summary: The study describes the photo-induced atomic layer deposition (photo-ALD) of tantalum oxide thin films using Ta(OC2H5)5 and O2 as precursors. The process was carried out in a temperature range of 170-350°C, with a self-limiting growth rate of 0.37 Å/cycle at 190-285°C. The films were amorphous, smooth, and exhibited high dielectric constants and low leakage current density, making them suitable for applications such as capacitors in DRAMs.
evidence: The growth of tantalum oxide thin films by photoinduced atomic layer deposition was investigated in the temperature range of 170-350°C using Ta(OC2H5)5 and O2 as precursors. A self-limiting growth rate of 0.37 Å/cycle was achieved at the substrate temperature range of 190-285°C. All the films grown in this temperature range were amorphous and very smooth. Electrical measurements performed on Pt/Ta2O5(10 nm)/Ru/SiO2/Si capacitors exhibited high dielectric constant (22-25) and a remarkably low leakage current density of 0.8 × 10−8 A/cm2 at an applied field of 1 MV/cm.
